cards.back: Non-mandatory recommendation (benchmark, advisory, implementation guide, reference architecture).
Mandatory, measurable requirement setting a minimum level: encryption, password length, physical configuration.
Known, approved minimum configuration serving as a compliance reference for a system.
Standard operating procedure: documented, repeatable sequence of steps for an operational task.
Task-oriented execution guide for operations: restart, failover, restore, verification.
BCP = continuity of business functions; DRP = restoration of IT systems and data.
Defines what is permitted or prohibited when using organizational resources and systems.
Sets conditions for using a personal device: enrollment, compliance, access, and revocation.
Prohibits leaving sensitive documents or media exposed on an unattended workstation.
Overarching policy stating management intent and general information security principles.
Defines authorities, reporting timelines, and obligations during an incident.
Defines data sensitivity levels and their retention periods.
States principles for granting, reviewing, and revoking access.
Describes data destruction methods and required proof of destruction.
Specifies who and how to report a vulnerability, and within what timeframe.
Explains collection, use, retention, and individuals' rights over their data.
Need/owner → drafting/review → approval → distribution/acknowledgment → review and versioning.
IETF specification document, cited in §5.1 as a de facto external standard.
